scope: Restore the authorized Domain/OS VM display if idle, inspect the actual mouse route, and attempt a bounded relative-pointer visual checkpoint without pressing any scrollbar target until its position is visible.

vm.reference: Domain/OS SR10.4 + HP VUE 2.01, Apollo DN3500, MAME 0.276

actions.name: screen wake
actions.result: The native guest framebuffer was black. Sent one Shift frame via :kbd:keyboard4/Shift, auto-cleared by frame 3; native capture at frame 65 showed VUE, Terminal, Trash Can, and both scrollbars.

actions.name: pointer checkpoint
actions.result: One bounded +X step then six -X steps were injected via the existing helper; each operation finished and cleared its counter overrides without cleanup error. Captures did not show the pointer; the one-step image differences were confined to the advancing panel clock. No click/hold was sent to a scrollbar.

evidence.board_scripts_record: Board scripts-record attached to I167 revision 2; 12 Lua scripts recorded; no source-code change in this VM-control step.

result: The VM is awake and stable. The current capture-off route did not produce a visible pointer after the bounded counter steps, so the horizontal held-state target cannot be confirmed. This does not establish a scrollbar defect.
limits: No horizontal button press was attempted because the native image did not confirm the pointer over the target.
No host capture, mouse-device option, input sequences, focus, VM disk, or performance profile were changed.
The direct counter helper test is not proof that guest mouse input is routed when capture is disabled.
next: Keep I167 running. Ask whether to use a different authorized input route for the horizontal held-state comparison; do not alter the mouse capture hook or mapping without that decision.
